title: The realness predicate
content: Instead of using Mathlib's `Complex.im z = 0`, the proof defines `IsReal z` as the existence of a real `r` with `z = (r : ℂ)`. This existential form is exactly what makes the closure proofs one-liners: a witness for the product is the product of the witnesses, with no appeal to imaginary parts or conjugation.

title: Realness is closed under × and ÷
content: The only structural facts the whole theorem needs: if `z` and `w` are real then so are `z * w` and `z / w`. Each proof destructs the witnesses `z = a`, `w = b` and supplies `a * b` (resp. `a / b`) as the new witness, closing with `push_cast; ring`. Division works even when `w = 0` because `a / 0 = 0` is still real in ℂ.
mathContext: $z = a,\ w = b \ \Rightarrow\ z\cdot w = ab,\quad z / w = a/b$

title: The cross-ratio
content: The cross-ratio of four points is the projective invariant at the heart of the proof. It is `noncomputable` because it divides in ℂ. Its conformal invariance — preserved by Möbius transformations — is what lets a single algebraic quantity detect concyclicity.

title: Concyclicity and collinearity as realness
content: The classical criterion: four points are concyclic-or-collinear exactly when their cross-ratio is real, and three points are collinear exactly when the ratio `(a-c)/(b-c)` is real. Encoding the geometry this way reduces every circle/line incidence in the theorem to a single realness assertion, which is then manipulated purely algebraically.

title: The pivot theorem (conditional form)
content: The sharp conditional statement: given the three side-incidences `Z ∈ AB`, `X ∈ BC`, `Y ∈ CA` and a point `M` already on circles `(AYZ)` and `(BZX)`, conclude `M` lies on `(CXY)`. Eight nondegeneracy hypotheses (distinctness of the relevant points) are made explicit so the denominators never vanish. This form deliberately avoids constructing the Miquel point as a circle-circle intersection.

title: Clearing the denominators
content: Each distinctness hypothesis is turned into a nonvanishing difference via `sub_ne_zero.mpr`. These eight `≠ 0` facts are precisely the denominators that `field_simp` must discharge when it clears the three cross-ratio fractions in the key identity.

title: Pivot cancellation — the algebraic miracle
content: The crux of the entire proof: the product of the three Miquel cross-ratios is *independent of the pivot* `M`. Every factor containing `M` cancels, leaving a quantity built only from the triangle and the three side points. After unfolding `crossRatio`, a single `field_simp` proves the identity — the geometry has been compressed into one rational equation.

title: The product is real
content: The three right-hand factors are exactly the collinearity ratios for `Z ∈ AB`, `X ∈ BC`, `Y ∈ CA`, so each is real by hypothesis and their product is real by the closure lemma. Rewriting through `key`, the cross-ratio product inherits this realness. The first two cross-ratios are also shown nonzero, which is needed for the final division.

title: The third cross-ratio is a quotient of reals
content: Final step: `M` on the first two circles makes the first two cross-ratios real, and their product is nonzero. Writing the third cross-ratio as (whole product) ÷ (first two) via `eq_div_iff`, it becomes a quotient of two reals — hence real — so `M` lies on the third circle `(CXY)`. No complex conjugation is ever used.
